subject: Operations
title: Nearshoring to Neighbors
description: A fast breakdown of Nearshoring to Neighbors for builders.

hook.text: Instead of shipping from China, a US firm moves production to Mexico. Same time zone, shorter supply chain, lower risk.

buildup.text: Nearshoring moves operations to nearby countries—close enough for short lead times but cheap enough for cost savings.

discovery.text: Mexico, Eastern Europe, and Turkey have become nearshoring hubs for the US, Western Europe, and the Middle East.

twist.text: Nearshoring isn't always cheaper than offshoring. The value is in shorter lead times, easier visits, and reduced risk.

climax.text: Mexico surpassed China as the top US import source in 2023—nearshoring is reshaping global trade patterns.

punchline.text: Close enough to visit. Far enough to save.

quiz.question: Why is Mexico becoming a nearshoring hub for the US?
